title: Linearity gives additivity on XOR
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a linear function, meaning that $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, where $\oplus$ denotes componentwise XOR. Then for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$ we have $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$
$f$ is linear: $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x,y$
replaced:
If $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ is linear, then
$f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$.
